title: Adaptive fragment resurrection + kernel-hinting protocol for paged KV
creator: Aria Patel
description: Goal: reduce prefill miss rate and avoid repeated fragment churn by introducing a lightweight 'fragment resurrection' layer combined with kernel-hint vectors to guide kernel selection. The feature proactively keeps high-value fragments available for impending decodes and informs the kernel selector about fragment density so it can choose an execution path optimized for sparse vs dense page layouts. This ticket covers design, prototype, microbench evaluation, and an incremental canary rollout in staging.
background: Current paged-attention workload exhibits repeated eviction/reload cycles for medium hot fragments (~2-8KB). This creates decoding stalls and forces suboptimal kernel choices that assume either fully-in-memory KV pages or cold streaming. Prior work (see ENG-231456 and ENG-272459) improved affinity routing and prefill admission, but we still see a 12-22% prefill miss tail depending on tenant mix. We hypothesize a resurrection + hinting approach reduces redundant restores and allows the kernel selector to pick kernels with lower per-token overhead for fragmented pages.
design_decision_summary: Introduce three cooperating mechanisms: (1) micro-reservation tokens: short-lived soft-reservations for fragments predicted to be reused within the next N decodes; (2) resurrector: a background worker that opportunistically rehydrates evicted fragments using a probabilistic reuse predictor (lightweight LRU augmented with bloom-based prefix-match); (3) kernel-hint vector: a compact descriptor (fragment density, avg decode window, reuse score) attached to shard metadata and passed to kernel selector. Trade-offs: extra memory pressure from soft-reservations vs reduced decode stalls; modest CPU for resurrector vs throughput gains.
acceptance_criteria: 1) p95 decode latency improves or stays flat with a reduction in prefill-miss-rate by >=12% on our mixed synthetic workload; 2) KV thrash rate decreases by >=15% for medium-hot fragments; 3) no regression in p99 under high-concurrency (stress) tests; 4) integration tests for kernel-hint API and resurrector telemetry in infra-metrics.
implementation_notes: Prototype in runtime/growth/kv_resurrector. Add kernel_hint struct to kernel-pick API (backwards compatible flag). Resurrector uses tenant-weighted admission and max soft-reserve budget per shard. Hard-limit enforcement will be gated behind feature flag 'kv_resurrector_v1'. Use existing warmup path for page load to avoid duplicating IO logic.
benchmark_plan: Microbench: two-tier synthetic workload (short chat-like prefixes and long context doc ingestion). Metrics: prefill_miss_rate, kv_eviction_rate, decode_p50/p95/p99, throughput (tokens/s), memory_headroom. Run baseline vs resurrector enabled with kernel hints; run with 50/75/100% load profiles and at different quantization kernels.
comments: 2025-11-05 - Aria: Initial design draft posted; flagged potential memory pressure for multi-tenant hosts. Need a tenant fairness cap.
2025-11-06 - Marco: Prototype started. Added soft-reserve token counter to shard state. Observed ~4% extra GPU memory accounting in local dev when soft-reserve budget=2MB/shard.
2025-11-07 - PM Review (Lena Ortiz): Strong thumbs-up on user-facing metrics. Asked for clear rollback plan and metric thresholds for canary.

2025-11-09 - Design Review (Noah Kim): Suggested replacing bloom prefix-match with count-min for lower false-positive cost; we decided to keep bloom due to memory-access patterns and fast SIMD bloom checks.

2025-11-10 - Marco: Ran microbench v1. Result: prefill-miss-rate down 11.6% and decode p95 down 6% in mixed workload. CPU usage for resurrector worker at 3-4% of single core. Pushing changes to PR for internal review.

2025-11-12 - QA: Added stress test that creates rapid fragment churn across 120 tenants. Observed a p99 regression when soft-reserve budget > 8MB/shard; we will cap per-shard soft-reserve to 4MB by default and make configurable.
2025-11-12 - Next steps: refine resurrector admission policy, add kernel_hint telemetry, run A/B canary in staging for 48h with rollback thresholds.
Reviewer feedback: include delta-tracing hooks to map a decoded request to the resurrected fragment lifecycle for debugging (link to infra trace RFC).
notes_for_rollout: Canary staged via capacity-split routing. Initial rollout only to non-enterprise tenants in us-west. Canary monitors: prefill_miss_rate_delta, decode_p95_delta, kv_memory_headroom, resurrector_cpu_pct. Automatic rollback if decode_p95 increases >5% or prefill_miss_rate improves less than 5% after 12h.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Add resurrector metrics to long-term retention; 2) Evaluate count-min alternative (per Noah's note) under memory-limited nodes; 3) Integrate with autoscaler hints so resurrector backs off under GPU memory pressure; 4) Document kernel-hint schema for third-party kernel vendors.
audit_trail: Design doc v1 -> prototype -> microbench -> QA stress -> staging canary. PR: runtime#4892 references this ticket and includes unit tests for soft-reserve accounting.
estimated_impact_statement: If successful, expected to reduce tail decode latency and lower per-token CPU waste by avoiding repeated page IOs. We estimate a 5-15% net throughput improvement for mixed chat/document workloads with comparable unit cost.
remarks: Avoid enabling resurrector for tenants with strict memory isolation policies until per-tenant budgeting has been validated. Feature flag controlled rollout planned.
